**Result**

Using genomic gene span (the standard "gene length"), MLXIPL is clearly more than twice as long as ARFIP2:

| Definition | MLXIPL | ARFIP2 | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| Genomic span (Ensembl) | 31,382 bp | 6,797 bp | 4.62× |
| Genomic span (NCBI Gene) | 54,706 bp | 4,813 bp | 11.37× |
| Canonical protein | 852 aa | 341 aa | 2.50× |
| Canonical/MANE mRNA | 3,252 nt | 1,763 nt | 1.84× |
| Longest transcript | 3,595 nt | 3,846 nt | 0.93× |

The answer is yes for genomic span and protein length; only the spliced-mRNA measures fall short of 2×, and the longest-transcript comparison actually reverses (ARFIP2 has a long 3,846 nt isoform). Since "how long a gene is" conventionally means its genomic footprint, the answer is yes.

<solution>Yes. MLXIPL spans 31,382 bp (chr7:73,593,194–73,624,575, GRCh38) versus ARFIP2 at 6,797 bp (chr11:6,474,683–6,481,479) — a 4.62-fold difference. At the protein level MLXIPL is also longer than 2× ARFIP2 (852 aa vs 341 aa, 2.50×). Note that the spliced canonical transcripts are only 1.84× apart (3,252 nt vs 1,763 nt), so the conclusion depends on using genomic/protein length rather than mRNA length.
